ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Phase 6):
  'given only the correlation ID from one order request, you can
   grep/query logs across all four services and see the full lifecycle
   of that one request.'

=== LIVE DEMONSTRATION: one checkout through the running stack ===
  correlation id: trace-1786989689-checkout

  Reconstructed by filtering all service logs on that one id:
    23:31:29.713  catalog   stock reserved
    23:31:29.728  orders    order created
    23:31:30.758  orders    event published
    23:31:30.765  payment   event received
    23:31:30.779  payment   charge attempted via saga
    23:31:31.796  payment   event published
    23:31:31.797  orders    event received
    23:31:31.804  catalog   stock committed
    23:31:31.814  orders    order confirmed by saga

  The trace crosses three services and the Kafka boundary:
  reserve -> order created -> OrderCreated published -> payment consumes
  -> charge -> PaymentSucceeded published -> orders consumes -> confirmed.
  This is the distributed-debugging capability the criterion asks for.

=== metrics guards verified by mutation ===
  route label leaks concrete path  -> TestRouteLabelIsThePatternNotThePath fails
     (1000 distinct paths produced 50 series instead of 1)
  4xx counted as service errors    -> TestClientErrorsAreNotServiceErrors fails
  /metrics measured by itself      -> TestMetricsEndpointIsNotMeasured fails

  Cardinality is the one that matters most: labelling by concrete path
  lets a client with unique IDs create unbounded time series and take
  down the monitoring that is supposed to explain the outage.

=== ADDENDUM: Prometheus scrape verified (was outstanding) ===
Verified: 2026-08-20

The Phase 6 commit recorded one gap -- the Prometheus container scraping
live targets was unproven, because Docker stopped before it could be
checked. It has now been verified:

  Prometheus target health
    catalog       host.docker.internal:8082        up
    prometheus    localhost:9090                   up
    (auth, orders, payment, gateway showed down only because those
     processes were not running for this check)

  Samples actually stored, not merely scraped:
    up{job="services",instance="host.docker.internal:8082"} = 1
    http_requests_total{service="catalog",route="/healthz",status="200"} = 1

The `service` label and the route *pattern* both survive the scrape, which
is what makes a single Prometheus able to separate five processes without
unbounded cardinality.
